items.title: Artemis Fowl Animated TV Show Greenlit With Eoin Colfer as Executive Producer
items.excerpt: Artemis Fowl is coming back to TV screens in the form of an animated show on Disney Channel and Disney+.
items.content_text: Artemis Fowl is coming back to TV screens in the form of an animated show on Disney Channel and Disney+. Author Eoin Colfer announced that Disney had greenlit another series project based on his family fantasy novels at the 25 Years of Artemis Fowl panel at New York Comic Con 2026. He'll remain involved in the animated show as an executive producer, too, with Disney promising that he'll bring "his creative vision to dig deeper into the characters and lore of the beloved book series that is celebrating its 25th anniversary of the first book this year." Joining Colfer in the executive producing category is Marvel's Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur's Ben Juwono, as well as DuckTales' Colleen Evanson. In a statement, the Artemis Fowl author said he is "proud and delighted to be part of the formidable team that is putting the Artemis Fowl animation on screen." "Everyone is so talented and so positive that I feel certain the fairy world is in excellent hands," he added. The Artemis Fowl animated series has no release date, but when it does eventually arrive, it won't be the first swing at the property to land on Disney+. In 2020, Disney launched a live-action movie with the same name , though it largely failed to leave a good impression on fans or critics. As recorded by review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes , the straight-to-streaming film only whipped up a "rotten" 8% from critics and 19% from audiences. The Artemis Fowl movie starred Ferdia Shaw as its title character and also featured appearances from Lara McDonnell, Josh Gadd, and Michael Rouse. IGN called it "an empty science fantasy tale with forgettable characters and an uninspired story" in our 4/10 review . In other words, a crack at a film didn't quite pan out, but where the 2020 project failed, the new animated show hopes to succeed. "The action-adventure fantasy series Artemis Fowl follows 13-year-old genius Artemis Fowl as he uncovers an underground world of armed and dangerous — and surprisingly high-tech — fairies as he launches a plan to capture one and steal its magic to heal his dying mom and save his family," a description said. The original Artemis Fowl book was published in 2001, with the rest of Colfen's stories in the universe boasting more than 35 million copies sold across the globe. Elsewhere at NYCC 2026, we got another solid look at both Godzilla Minus Zero and Blade Runner 2099 . More Naruto was confirmed to be on the way , too.

items.title: Resident Evil Overtakes Weapons as Zach Cregger's Highest-Grossing Film, The Social Reckoning Bombs
items.excerpt: Resident Evil beat Weapons to become Zach Cregger's highest-grossing film while The Social Reckoning bombed at the box office.
items.content_text: Resident Evil beat Weapons to become director Zach Cregger's highest-grossing film while The Social Reckoning bombed at the box office. The live-action adaptation of Capcom's classic survival horror series turned heads as it reached an estimated worldwide total of $320.2 million over the weekend. With $138.5 million domestically and $181.7 million internationally, Resident Evil has officially cleared Weapons' $270 million with a few weeks and change to spare. Cregger brought his re-imagined Raccoon City to the big screen on September 18, 2026, making this weekend its fourth in theaters. The massive jump – which saw it return to the number one spot, globally – was largely propelled by its premiere in China. Of the whopping $62.65 million it accumulated through weekend four, $40.6 million was earned in China alone. Its victory over Weapons already seemed secure, but as it stands atop Cregger's catalog, it's also continuing to leave its reported $75 million budget in the dust. Resident Evil's ongoing success in theaters kicked off when it brought in $108.3 million in its opening weekend. It was a strong start that even managed to bleed over into the gaming world with increased sales for some of the games, too, with Cregger's latest also landing as the highest-rated video game adaptation of all time. It's hard to imagine the film's release going any better than it did, especially considering the months leading up to its premiere were plagued by negativity online. Gaming fans spent much of their time talking about the movie's lack of recognizable characters and its tweaks to the lore, with Cregger arguing that he made the changes in order to make a better movie . By just about every measure, it seems the bet paid off. These mid-October box office results show signs of an audience ready for Halloween, with Other Mommy also performing well despite poor reviews from both critics and audiences alike (via Rotten Tomatoes ). Sitting with an abysmal 18% critic score and 47% audience score, Jessica Chastain's new horror movie landed in second place globally with 45.19 million (27.5 million domestically, $17.69 million internationally). As bone-chilling trailers convinced scary movie fans to show up for an unnerving performance, there were also some notable losers in theaters, too. Tom Cruise's Digger continued its unfortunate run with $9.6 million in weekend two, marking a 48% drop for a total of $35.3 million. The true disappointment, though, was Aaron Sorkin's The Social Network sequel, The Social Reckoning. Starring Jeremy Allen White and Mikey Madison, and including Jeremy Strong's performance as Mark Zuckerberg, the film's opening weekend saw it open in seventh place with just $9 million. At $5.5 million domestically and $17.69 million internationally on a reported budget of $30 million (via Variety ), The Social Reckoning is a certified bomb. It's a painful reality for the Facebook movie follow-up, especially after Jesse Eisenberg's original picture ended its run with $224.9 million (via Box Office Mojo ) and plenty of praise. The Social Reckoning could always stand the test of time, but with a Rotten Tomatoes score of 55% from critics and 74% from audiences, it's not looking good. October still has plenty to give, though. Capcom's live-action Street Fighter movie and Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything will both release next weekend, October 16. DC body horror movie Clayface then follows October 23. For the movies you can see in theaters now, be sure to check out IGN's reviews. We called Resident Evil "Great" with an 8/10 and Other Mommy "Bad" with a 4/10 . We talked about the highs and lows of Digger in our 6/10 review for the Cruise film, while The Social Reckoning returned a 7/10 .

items.title: New NetEase FPS Sparks Warzone 'Rip-Off' Claims, But Some Call of Duty Fans Are Happy to See It
items.excerpt: Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players.
items.content_text: Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players. NetEase called its new shooter a "self-developed extreme-sports tactical shooter" when revealing it just days ago. It's yet another big swing from the China-based tech company that boasts breakneck gameplay on PC via Steam and mobile devices, but in the hours since its big debut, it's also been called a "1:1 rip" of Activision's Call of Duty: Warzone, and it's not too hard to see why. Viewers say guns look, kick, and move in a way that seems familiar, but the similarities don't stop there. Everything down the UI is being investigated by FPS enjoyers, too, with things like the sound effects also evoking the same kind of gritty action Call of Duty is known for. Even the way the first-person camera blurs when dropping from heights might feel familiar to fans of Warzone and other shooters. Even with characters that present their own unique abilities and gadgets, ECC: Redline has had a hard time escaping the comparisons online. Introducing ECC: REDLINE, an extreme-sports tactical shooter. Welcome to the Extreme Circuit Championship. Enter the Circuit, Own the Edge. Wishlist now on Steam: https://t.co/zy0dnkBGQn #ECCREDLINE #ECC https://t.co/TL7c3fAoAX — ECC (@ECCREDLINE) October 9, 2026 "Warzone + Delta Force + Blood Strike = ECC: Redline," one YouTube comment left on NetEase's official upload said . "It’s 1-to-1 Warzone, hilarious s**t," another commenter on Reddit said . "Literally the first thing that popped into my head was wow they have no shame," another replied , "straight copied COD even down to the UI and emblems etc." Meanwhile, Call of Duty has faced its own struggles in the six years since the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare reboot introduced Warzone in 2019. Like so many other popular ongoing FPS experiences, the battle royale offshoot's popularity has ebbed and flowed, with many of its millions of fans often still calling back to its launch build and its first map, Verdansk, as the glory days. This looks about as close of a 1:1 rip of Warzone as someone could legally get away with — ModernWarzone (@ModernWarzone) October 9, 2026 This is Warzone with player abilities and some blatant CoD rips😂 — Jake Lucky (@JakeSucky) October 10, 2026 @iKaito_1 similar? its literally copy and paste — 👾 (@Axie_Umami) October 9, 2026 Activision has returned to Verdansk in an attempt to recapture that magic , but it's done little to calm those nostalgic for the past. As the broader Call of Duty brand goes through its own struggles , some players – even those willing to admit NetEase may have gone too far in a few places – say a polished-looking shooter like ECC: Redline could scratch a pretty specific itch. Some even believe the NetEase shooter could give Call of Duty a run for its money. "If ECC: Redline actually has good servers, movement, AND listens to its community… COD might finally have to start trying again," one post on X/Twitter said . "Close enough, welcome back OG Warzone," another player said , acknowledging the similarities before saying the NetEase game "looks better tbh." Looks like someone reverse-engineered OG Warzone and added character abilities. I’m actually kinda interested in trying this 😅 — Westie (@MrProWestie) October 10, 2026 Warzone don’t have ability 🥳! Netease definitely might pull this one off lol https://t.co/oHFmquZoTK — Ju banks (@banks_ju) October 9, 2026 @ModernWarzone So what? I'd rather spend it on a ripoff game who listens to their customers then a conglomerate who 💩 on them. — 𝗥𝗶𝗴 𝕏 (@RigTate) October 10, 2026 "I LEGIT thought it was WZ at first because i didn't check the title," one social media user said , adding a crying emoji. NetEase has faced criticism regarding its approach to previous games in the past. A less extreme example is Marvel Rivals , a comic book hero shooter that exploded with popularity – and also managed to pick up some comparisons to Blizzard Entertainment's Overwatch – when it launched in 2024. On the other hand is Hyper Front, a 5v5 tactical shooter that Riot Games launched a lawsuit against after it drew comparisons to Valorant. ECC: Redline currently has no release date but is being billed as a free-to-play game. Warzone, meanwhile, is slated to receive a slew of new updates when Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches later this month.

items.title: Tekken 8 Yujiro Teaser Reveals Baki Rep's In-Game Render Is Just as Uncanny as Fans Expected
items.excerpt: Bandai Namco has revealed a first look at Tekken 8 DLC character Yujiro Hanma, and the Baki rep is looking just as uncanny as fans expected.
items.content_text: Bandai Namco has revealed a first look at Tekken 8 DLC character Yujiro Hanma, and the Baki rep is looking just as uncanny as fans expected. The new trailer for the fighting game's Season 3 characters debuted alongside Evo France 2026. Following Kunimitsu's release in June and Bob's release in August, kangaroo-and-joey fighter Roger Jr. is now officially set for a November 11 early access launch, with the full release following November 16, but the character most fans are looking forward to is still without a proper release date. Roger Jr. is definitely the star of the new Tekken 8 DLC trailer, with nearly three minutes of its four-minute runtime dedicated to showing off the marsupial boxer's gameplay. The Yujiro teaser, meanwhile, is tucked at the end, but its reveals are particularly shocking. You can see how the Baki the Grappler villain has been reimagined within the world of Tekken below. Yujiro is… expressive, to say the least, so nailing his face and bulging muscles was always going to draw attention. Well, the Bandai Namco team did their best, with today's Evo trailer showing just a few shots of his iconic toothy smile and flexibility. It looks like work on the anime guest character is still underway, but just because there's no release date doesn't mean there isn't a plan to show more. The end of the new teaser promised that a new Yujiro trailer will premiere alongside the Tekken World Tour Finals January 17, 2027. That's three months out from now, so we can probably expect to see gameplay by that point. Looking back at the calendar, Bandai Namco has typically had a few months of downtime between Tekken 8 DLC releases. It will have been two months since Roger Jr. was released when the Yujiro trailer is shared, meaning we can also expect a release date announcement around that time, too. If we're lucky, the Baki fighter might even drop that same day, but again, nothing regarding his release date has been confirmed quite yet. Roger Jr. and Yujiro are both included in the Season 3 pass and will round out its promise of four bonus characters. Season 1 and Season 2 included fighters like Heihachi, Armor King, Anna, and Final Fantasy 16 protagonist Clive Rosfield. While passes cost $30 each, the Season 3 pass is currently available for $34.99. IGN learned more about Yujiro's inclusion in Tekken 8 when speaking with producer Naoya Yasuda and director of promotions and former Baki manga editor Yuki Yokoi earlier this year. Be sure to read the full interview for insight into how and why the team decided to include a character that never loses. You can also read about how former Tekken director Katsuhiro Harada influenced one of Roger Jr.'s best references , and the player who climbed through the ranks while blindfolded .

items.title: ‘I’m Shocked That People Are Still Playing’ – How GTA 5 Took Over the World
items.excerpt: Could GTA 6 be as big as its predecessor? We take a look at how GTA 5 became one of the biggest games in history, selling over 230m copies and being played by millions of people every week for over a decade.
items.content_text: There are over 230 million copies of Grand Theft Auto 5 in the world. As the second-highest selling game of all time, it has been played for billions of hours by players across the globe, making it one of the most significant pastimes in the entire world. That’s an impressive achievement for what in 2013 was simply the highly-anticipated next entry in Rockstar’s beloved (and notorious) open-world crime series. But GTA 5 proved to be much, much more than a typical sequel. It has become home to a huge, expressive, and loyal community, one which has made a digital hobby of everything from warring alien clans to producing slick vehicle stunt movies. This is the story of how a video game became much more than a crime simulator. Ash Skyqueen’s avatar weaves between the traffic of busy Dorset Drive on a motorbike spouting flames. Suddenly she veers, mounting the pavement at high speed and rebounding from the roof of a bus stop to achieve incredible air. Momentum carries her through a perfect circle, barely bigger than a human body, that forms the second ‘O’ of the ‘LIQUOR HOLE’ store sign. Pulling the ripcord of her parachute, she lands with a slight stagger at the door of the rundown booze establishment on Eclipse Boulevard - a couple of streets over from where her jump began. It’s the first feat in a stunt montage which Ash put together to celebrate ten years of GTA 5 – the game that gave her freedom, companionship and goals when she was robbed of all three. “I’d had a ruptured disc in my spine, so I was bed bound shortly after the game came out,” she says. “All day every day for about three years straight, it became my therapy in a way. You’re stuck in bed, can’t do anything, can’t work, no social life, a pretty miserable existence. And then I’m suddenly connected to a community of people doing the same thing. It kept me from going insane.” It’s a striking demonstration of why GTA 5 has remained a deeply important game to millions of players. A pillar of pop culture, it was erected in 2013 and has loomed over the entertainment industries during every year since. Thanks to the enduring love for its single-player story campaign and its ever-popular, seemingly invincible online mode, GTA 5 has spanned three console generations and made around $10 billion dollars for publisher Take-Two – over 3 times more than the highest-grossing movie ever. When Shawn Levy and Ryan Reynolds made Free Guy, a Hollywood comedy about the social connection and wanton violence of online games, it was GTA they chose to riff on. Where previous Grand Theft Auto entries were cinema-riffing crime simulators that routinely broke sales records, GTA 5 has evolved beyond those confines. It has become an alternate world where players can escape to a funhouse mirror version of LA – the most mythologised city on the planet. There they become whoever they want to be: stunt specialist, bank robber, nightclub kid, hitchhiker or filmmaker. The GTA Campaign, Re-Tuned In some ways, GTA 5 was a course correction for Rockstar. While 2008’s Grand Theft Auto 4 had been rapturously received, it was a narrower interpretation of what the series could be. Some players chafed against its dour and grounded tone, as well as the unforgiving driving simulation that threatened to hurl speeding players through the windscreen. It was a largely straight-faced vision that left a space for rivals like Saints Row developer Volition, who filled the vacuum with gleefully absurd city sandboxes populated by dildo-toting gangsters and gimp chariots. GTA 5, however, saw Rockstar reclaim its lost territory in the single-player space without compromising its serious storytelling chops. The developer turned up all the dials on its screaming satire, filling its campaign missions with ludicrous plane, train, and helicopter setpieces in which the bodies hit the floor without moral consequence. The driving was made friendlier, and the oppressive skyscrapers of GTA 4 replaced by the open freeways of the San Andreas countryside. Yet GTA 5 also told the ambitious tale of three controllable protagonists at totally different points in their lives – Franklin, the young and hungry Scarface-in-waiting; Michael, the washed-up cuckold; and Trevor, the psychopathic embodiment of the five-star Wanted level. As clear as that ambition is to see in the final product, Mike York had nothing close to a sense of that full picture when he first joined the GTA 5 development team as an animator, two and a half years before its launch. “A lot of times during production you’re thrown in there, and you don’t know what the story is and how it plays out,” he says. “There are a lot of scenes where I didn’t even know what came before or after. I was so out of the loop with the story of the game. They just threw me a cutscene with Tanisha and Franklin and were like, ‘Hey, can you do the body animation on this?’ But I had no idea how it connected. All I knew is, ‘Damn, this girl looks mad at Franklin. She looks like she just broke up with him.’” Even in the final six months of development, when members of the team were “all hands on deck” and testing the game for eight hours every day, it was impossible to perceive GTA 5 in its entirety. “As a tester, you’re trying to play through the whole game over and over and over again,” York says. “But the game is very long. A lot of times I would play the game from the very beginning, up until 60% or 70%, and then a new build of the game would come out where they fixed a bunch of bugs. And so I only played the game from start to finish all the way one time, and that was after I was done from the project and played it at my house by myself.” I was shocked about how massive it was, how big the world was, and how cool it was to switch characters. Only then could York finally appreciate the enormous puzzle he’d been contributing pieces to for so long. “I think the biggest thing I was shocked about was how massive it was, how big the world was, and how cool the system was of being able to switch characters,” he says. “I thought that was unique, and I knew that players hadn’t seen that before.” It’s a system that Rockstar’s peers in the triple-A sphere are only now catching up to - infusing Spider-Man 2 and Assassin’s Creed Shadows with swappable protagonists whose stories are entwined. As an American, York appreciated Rockstar North’s Scottish perspective - an outsider’s view of the quirks and comedy inherent in LA culture. “I think they have a pretty good eye, a good touch on our society,” he says. “And that’s because, even though the main studio is in Edinburgh, a lot of the people that work there are from the US, or all they do is watch US TV shows and play US games. They’re engulfed in our culture in general. So even though they live in the UK, they have a good pulse on everything that’s going around here.” When the midnight launch came, Ash Skyqueen and her sister stood in line at the Metrocentre shopping mall in the north-east of England. Like so many others, she took the game home and pushed it straight into the console. Behind the scenes, the development team were “stoked, walking around the office and telling people, ‘Oh my God, did you see we just sold this many?’ There were a lot of funny comments from people on YouTube channels and we were all geeking out about that.” Simultaneously, however, Rockstar was readying to launch GTA Online - the platform that would take Los Santos multiplayer. “We were trying to get prepared for that, too,” York says. “So half of it is excitement, and the other half is trying to get some stuff done for Online.” The Live-Service Frontier GTA Online arrived only two weeks after its parent game and immediately ran into problems. There were difficulties with servers, crashes and lost character progress. The IGN review of the time criticised the repetitive missions and oddly mute player avatars, who contributed little to cutscenes with established GTA characters like Trevor. “I’m left with the overbearing impression,” wrote Keza MacDonald, “that Grand Theft Auto Online as it stands right now is still a colour sketch of what it will probably one day become.” In 2017, Rockstar’s then director of design, Imran Sarwar, offered an unusually frank assessment of GTA Online’s formative period. “To be totally honest it did not begin very well at all,” he told Game Informer . “It’s one of our biggest regrets that we lost millions of players in that first year that have never experienced how much we have improved and added to the game since the early days.” It’s one of our biggest regrets that we lost millions of players in that first year. Rockstar had promised players cooperative heists – huge multistage missions featuring lavish story sequences in the mode of single-player GTA. But the company’s first attempts didn’t live up to its own standards and had to be redesigned from scratch, leading to several delays. “GTA Online was slowly failing - and quickly losing players - right up until the middle of 2014,” Sarwar said. “The updates were not interesting enough, and as a company we did not realise how challenging it was going to be to have a team that essentially ran a content service, not make normal games.” This is not the obvious oversight it might seem today. When GTA Online launched, the live service model was in its nascency. Fortunately, as Rockstar fumbled around trying to figure out the shape of its multiplayer platform, it had a critically acclaimed single-player game to lean on. “GTA 5 helped prop up GTA Online in the early days when Rockstar was still exploring how it wanted the online component to work,” says James McWhirter, senior games analyst at Omdia. “There was a lot of experimentation going on behind the scenes.” Some of those experiments were in economics. If there’s a comparison to be drawn, it’s Team Fortress 2 – the competitive FPS that Valve used as a testing ground for new business models that have since become standard in Counter-Strike, Dota 2, and a host of other games besides. Ultimately, GTA 5 has made its billions through multiple different methods. “It’s simultaneously pulling all of those levers,” McWhirter says. “You’ve got the upfront sales for GTA 5 itself, the full game. You’ve got in-game purchases via GTA Online, and now Rockstar have begun to lean into subscriptions with GTA+.” None of that would have panned out if the GTA Online team hadn’t solved its biggest creative problem: heists. As Rockstar began to update its world with unique new stories and complex missions that demanded coordination and mastery from their players, GTA Online genuinely started to look like the future of the series rather than a flawed spin-off. Even resolutely solo players braved the servers for fear of being left behind. “I was kind of shocked by how much extra story and missions they put into Online,” York says, who left Rockstar in 2017 – a few years before the likes of the Cayo Perico and Diamond Casino heists were added. “They really went all out, I felt, adding all kinds of stuff to do in there.” Online Superiority GTA Online’s turnaround and subsequent financial success came at the cost of single-player expansions. Actor Steven Ogg filmed scenes for a solo campaign that would have featured Trevor as an undercover agent, but it never emerged thanks to GTA Online sucking up many of the resources once earmarked for DLC. “I can’t speak for the company, obviously,” York says. “But I think that they wanted to do a little bit of both. And I think they did have strong intent with DLC stuff, but the Online just did better. That happens a lot at studios, where they’ll have a DLC lined up that they’ll have plans for, and then they’ll completely shut it down because they realise something else is way more important - or they don’t even know if that DLC is going to perform well at all. They’d rather just not take the risk on it.” Similar to Minecraft or Fortnite, it’s a virtual world first and foremost, and a game second. GTA Online effectively took the place of traditional expansions, becoming an endgame for solo players who had exhausted every mission and diversion in GTA 5. Unusually for newcomers to an MMO, they arrived with dozens of hours of investment in its world and characters. “You know the map and where the streets are,” York says. “You finally get your own character.” “I played it like a single-player expansion at first,” Ash Skyqueen says. “Played through everything I could by myself, and kept playing. The mechanics have always been what appeals, so it was easy to sit there and figure out what I could do.” It’s with this spirit of exploration that GTA’s developers and players outgrew the limitations of the series’ original premise. “The more comfortable we were pushing beyond the traditional GTA concepts and experimenting more freely, we were able to introduce things like Cunning Stunts, the Special Vehicle Races, and adversary modes like Power Play, Tiny Racers, or Slasher,” Sarwar told Game Informer . The backdrop of Los Santos, recognisable as a contemporary city only slightly adjacent to our own world, proved helpfully malleable. “One of the updates GTA Online brought in was a TrackMania style game, racing in the cloud with a top-down perspective, almost like Micro Machines,” McWhirter says. “That just wouldn’t have been possible in Red Dead Redemption. Anything with a real world analog can be realised in GTA Online, so it’s a much more potent canvas for content updates over a long period of time. Whereas Red Dead is a lot more tied to its fiction. You couldn’t have flying horses, like having flying cars added to GTA Online.” That flexibility has enabled Rockstar to transform GTA into a platform for many different kinds of experiences, capable of holding player attention indefinitely. “Similar to Minecraft or Fortnite, it’s a virtual world first and foremost, and a game second,” McWhirter says. “In terms of GTA Online, the racing updates with the crazy track editors are a good example of how content that could perhaps normally make for a standalone game became a bolt-on for GTA Online.” Over time, these bolt-ons have replaced smaller game releases in Rockstar’s catalogue, for better or worse. “I would consider GTA Online to be the modern day equivalent of the double-A titles that Take-Two used to push out between those blockbuster games,” McWhirter says. “If we go back to the PS3 and 360 generation, there were games like Rockstar Games Presents Table Tennis and Bully, which we don’t really see anymore because teams are busy making content for GTA Online instead. Because that’s more valuable for the publisher. It helps them buy time between major GTA releases.” More Than Multiplayer For players like Ash Skyqueen, a new content drop in GTA Online serves a dual purpose. Beyond the extra heists and missions to play through, every update is a toy box filled with fresh animations and props to be repurposed in fan-made movies. Skyqueen got into making machinima through her community of stunters, who made use of a modding tool named MenyooSP. “It gives you access to everything,” she says. “I can set up a secondary character, give it a list of actions and animations to carry out, and then manually control my character and do what I need to do.” In her own movies, Skyqueen is star, stuntperson and director - the latter role enabled by the official video editor Rockstar added to GTA 5 back in 2015. One of her most popular creations, the silent short film Siren , evokes the intro cutscene of GTA 3 – following a Bonnie and Clyde-esque couple who wreak havoc as the FIB closes in. In the climax, a pre-programmed prison bus travels down the freeway - before Ash swings in on her bike to take down the convoy. “There’s a lot of choreography involved,” she says. “I’ll often just sit there with a nine-hour long YouTube video of all the GTA story cutscenes, keeping my eye out for something that I can use in a different context.” 180,000 viewers have watched Siren. Almost a million people have watched her Liqour Hole stunt . And Skyqueen hopes Rockstar will implement some of MenyooSP’s innovations officially in GTA 6. “I know they take note of this kind of stuff, and they certainly have promoted work that’s been made with it.” The ongoing success of GTA 5 raises questions about its eventual fate, once Rockstar’s sequel launches in November 2026. Will the studio run two versions of GTA Online simultaneously, at the risk of cannibalising its own playerbase? If not, and the GTA Online audience is migrated to a new Floridian setting, how will Rockstar account for all the properties and vehicles players have paid for? “If a new online mode is a completely separate thing from GTA 5 Online, managing continuously between two live service games is something that is currently unproven and it could be fraught,” McWhirter says. “I think that’s probably the biggest risk for them.” The situation brings to mind the arrival of EverQuest 2 in the mid noughties, when developer Sony Online Entertainment discovered that players typically played just one MMO and stuck with it. In such a context, a sequel’s biggest threat can be its own predecessor. “I think GTA 5 is going to solidify as one of the greatest games in history,” York says. “I think its legacy is already etched. It was revolutionary in so many aspects - in character switching and story. I’m shocked that people are still playing GTA 5, and it goes to show you how good that game is.” While admitting to a certain amount of bias as a former member of the development team, York believes that GTA 5 will be bigger than its own sequel once the dust settles. “I feel like GTA 5 was something special in gaming culture and history, and it’s gonna leave a lasting mark,” he says. “Games will come and go around it. My intuition is that GTA 6 will come out, people will love it, but it won’t be GTA 5. And people will constantly compare it to GTA 5. It’s going to be the most nostalgic for people, it’s going to be the one that affected them most as kids. And so I just feel like GTA 5 is going to be the GTA to be remembered. It’s gonna supersede Vice City. This is the one that marked history.” For Ash Skyqueen, who can no longer drive around a city in real life, GTA 5 is much more than a game. “It gives me that little bit of freedom back that I lost with the injury,” she says. “Though it’s simulated, it has such a good feel to it. I’ll always get on at Christmas when they turn on the snow. You’re walking around the streets at night, and it gives you that same vibe as in real life. In other games it’s just an aesthetic. But you can feel that stillness that comes with a dark snowy night. I don’t know how they do it.” Jeremy Peel is a freelance journalist and friend to anyone who will look at photos of his dogs.
items.title_en: ‘I’m Shocked That People Are Still Playing’ – How GTA 5 Took Over the World

items.title: Marvel Tokon DLC Roadmap Reveals First Look at Jane Foster Thor, Venom and Jubilee Coming in 2027
items.excerpt: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls will continue its Year 1 DLC roadmap with Thor (Jane Foster) this winter, with two more characters coming in 2027.
items.content_text: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls will continue its Year 1 DLC roadmap with Thor (Jane Foster) this winter, with two more characters coming in 2027. Developer Arc System Works confirmed the lineup alongside Evo France 2026. The Jane Foster version of Asgard's God of Thunder is now officially set to follow Phoenix Cyclops after he releases November 2, 2026, with today's announcement coming with both a sneak peek at her Marvel Tokon model in Odin's Vault on Asgard. The clip doesn't show too much, only teasing that we'll probably see Jane fight off Loki while wielding Mjolnir when a proper gameplay trailer premieres at a later date. Arc System Works said she's scheduled to launch in Marvel Tokon "winter 2027," so expect to see her arrival sometime before March of next year. Despite some concerns from players that poor sales could jeopardize the Marvel fighting game's future, at least two more characters will arrive in spring and summer 2027, too. Yes, Spider-Man anti-hero and Symbiote menace Venom will finally join the roster in spring 2027. X-Men firecracker Jubilee will then follow in the summer of that year. While Cyclops and Thor are entering the fray as relatively lesser-known versions of themselves, Venom and Jubilee appear to be mostly straightforward. That means Marvel Tokon players will get to see them fight the rest of the tag-team fighting with and against the game's roster – which includes characters like Doctor Doom, Iron Man, Carnage, Magneto, and more – in Arc System Works' heightened style. Although the details surrounding each DLC release are unclear, the reveal trailer did at least confirm that Venom will also come with a stage based on the Symbiote home world of Klyntar. It's all part of the Year 1 Character and Stage Pass, which costs $34.99. A roadmap with some of the most beloved characters from Marvel history would usually be enough to have comic book and video game fans frothing at the mouth, but uncertainty surrounding the project might have some looking at the Evo announcement in a different light. Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls launched to strong reviews (a 9/10 from IGN) in August, but at least on PC, players have struggled. Its Steam launch brought mixed reviews from fans who complained of widespread technical issues and PlayStation Network requirements. Even as the developers almost immediately promised to investigate the issues, it didn't take long for the backlash to swell to the point that famed fighting game community member Maximilian Dood wrote off playing the PC version altogether . It only took a few days for Arc System Works to push out a fix for most players' issues , but as Steam player numbers still struggle to break even 1,000 concurrent users (via SteamDB ), even the developers have admitted earning back trust will be "extremely challenging." While Marvel Tokon's presence on PlayStation 5 seemed to go over well, director Kazuto Sekine eventually went on to apologize for the PC launch . The developers clearly have a game plan for at least up until summer 2027. While we wait to see how characters like Thor, Venom, and Jubilee will punch and kick their way into Marvel Tokon, you can read about the characters dataminers were expecting to see first .

items.title: Wildwood Review
items.excerpt: Review: Wildwood is an arresting, exciting fantasy epic made all the more impressive by the fact that it’s handmade and hand-animated, even if some story stumbles occasionally hold it back.
items.content_text: Wildwood is in theaters on October 23. There’s something wondrous about the transportive power of stop-motion animated films when they’re executed at the standard that Laika sets for themselves, and wonder is certainly the name of the game in Wildwood. Adapted from the first novel in Colin Meloy and Carson Ellis’ Wildwood Chronicles, Wildwood sees director Travis Knight and the craftspeople at Laika turning in a staggeringly beautiful and surprisingly dark fantasy adventure that boasts exciting action, enchanting and enchanted natural settings, and talking woodland creatures with jobs… and that’s all before the characters leave Portland to journey into Wildwood! Wildwood is most impressive in its scope. As the new recordholder for the longest-ever stop-motion animated film, Knight luxuriates in building out the mythology of Meloy and Ellis’ novels onscreen. As 13-year-old Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) and her classmate Curtis (Jacob Tremblay) find themselves on a mission into the magical forest realm of Wildwood to save Prue’s kidnapped baby brother Mac, the intricate web of societies, races, and systems that prop up the setting are endlessly fascinating to keep track of thanks in large part to just how gorgeous it all looks. Laika’s films always push the boundaries of what’s possible for stop-motion animation, and the jaw-dropping artistry on display in Wildwood sees them doing it again. From the intricately authentic rendering of Portland, through each of the different domains of the massive, mystical forest, Wildwood is fathomless in its attention to fine detail. Long stretches of the film achieve such a sense of immersion that, at its most effective, it’s easy to forget that Wildwood is a stop-motion film at all, a sensation that’s even more impressive when taking into account the wide array of fantasy trappings that Wildwood deploys. At times, it’s surprising just how far Knight is willing to push the envelope for what could look on the surface like a kid-friendly romp. The nature-centric magic and anthropomorphic characters Prue and Curtis come up against will no doubt feel familiar to any fans of portal fantasies like Spirited Away, Labyrinth or The Chronicles of Narnia (not to mention Laika’s own Coraline), but Knight leans into the storytelling economy afforded to him by those archetypes with confidence. The “just go with it” style of his approach to what he chooses to detail about the history of Wildwood leaves moments where the movie breezes through exposition feeling pretty inoffensive, especially in light of just how fully-realized the world feels by the end of the movie. Through it all, the stakes of the story feel very high thanks to the quickly cascading conflict Prue and Curtis’ actions set off once they cross into the wilderness. Losses feel real, setbacks have consequences and people die in this movie, and with some amount of frequency at that. At times, it’s surprising just how far Knight is willing to push the envelope for what could look on the surface like a kid-friendly romp. Sure, nothing here approaches the hellish nightmare fuel present in the R-rated, Phil Tippett-directed Mad God , but make no mistake: Wildwood more than earns its PG-13 rating. That doesn’t stop character motivations from being occasional stumbling blocks for Wildwood, though. As fantastical and well-conceived as Wildwood’s world is, protagonist Prue does sometimes feel lost in the shuffle. Prue’s a very modern 13-year-old girl who bristles against her granola mom and dad (Maya Erskine and Jake Johnson) and takes the full brunt of responsibility for losing her brother, giving the character plenty of weight to have to shoulder as more and more bravery and pluck is required of her. Peyton Elizabeth Lee’s performance is energetic and dynamic enough to keep Prue likable, but the script doesn’t find much room for her to be more specifically defined by anything other than the wrongs she’s trying to right. That may be partially by design, maybe to let younger audience members project themselves into her adventure, but it does leave Prue feeling less memorable than the world she’s adventuring through. The tabletop RPG-loving Curtis, still stuck on hot chocolate when his peers have moved on to coffee, plays out an expected “zero to hero” arc, with Jacob Tremblay handling the character’s comedic timing well. Wildwood’s story does take Curtis away from Prue for a lot of the movie, and the pacing tends to drag when we check back in with him and the heroic bandits he crosses paths with in enemy territory. While the record-breaking 131-minute runtime more than justifies itself from a purely visual standpoint, plot detours like this do occasionally leave Wildwood feeling a little long in the tooth. Growing her power within Wildwood is Alexandra (Carey Mulligan), a governess of the South Wood whose grief coming out of the movie’s shockingly macabre opening scene drives her towards equally dark choices as the story goes. Alexandra’s relationship to her grief is far more interesting and believable than her machinations to quell it, but Mulligan’s quavering, edgy performance is a consistent highlight. Some late effort is made to draw parallels between Alexandra and Prue’s parents, which could’ve made Alexandra an even more compelling antagonist, but those connections don’t feel properly seeded into the early scenes to be satisfying to consider later on. From Alexandra’s grief, though, Knight does have occasion to produce some of Wildwood’s most evocative imagery, and those gothic touches are a welcome contrast to the bright, teeming life which makes up the majority of the movie’s visual identity. What’s left to be desired by the main players is more than made up for by Wildwood’s excellently cast supporting roster of magical creatures and heroes. Mahershala Ali and Amandla Stenberg? Badass bandits! Richard E. Grant? An owl king named Owl Rex! Tom Waits? Rage-filled coyote soldier! Charlie Day? Cowardly turncoat coyote soldier! From everyone as big as Angela Bassett’s giant eagle General to as small as Awkwafina’s spunky rat Septima, the voice cast is a key aspect of Wildwood’s personality. The color each of these characters add into the mix, especially the ways the animal characters’ more base instincts peek through in their personalities, does as much to create a sense of place as any of the sun-dappled valleys or ivy-ridden ruins that Prue and Curtis traverse. As Prue and Curtis attempt to outwit Alexandra’s forces, Wildwood’s action is breathlessly staged. The early kidnapping of the baby brother Mac by a murder of Alexandra’s crows and the chase that ensues hints at some of the gonzo camera work that’s to follow, and once the real world’s in the rear view mirror, Knight draws from every corner of his meticulously-populated frames to add a surprising twist to a fight, or to increase the danger of being caught or killed. Knight also has a pretty judicious eye for when to lock the camera into a more grounded style of coverage, and when to let it off the chain. All that excitement is very effectively supported by composer Dario Marianelli’s score, a lively orchestral bedrock which is alternatingly lead by either folk string arrangements or more modern guitar sounds depending on the environment.

items.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Trailer Reveals Sneak Peek at King Ghidorah's Gravity Beams
items.excerpt: Toho's latest Godzilla Minus Zero trailer is here and puts the spotlight on King Ghidorah's lightning-like gravity beams and Godzilla's iconic atomic breath.
items.content_text: Toho's latest Godzilla Minus Zero trailer is here and puts the spotlight on King Ghidorah's lightning-like gravity beams and Godzilla's iconic atomic breath. This new sneak peek at the King of the Monsters and the latest iteration of his archnemesis debuted as part of New York Comic Con 2026. Toho refrained from showing its new design for Ghidorah yet again , but there's still plenty of new footage to see in the one-minute video. How did Noriko Oishi (Minami Hamabe) survive Godzilla's first attack? That's the question Godzilla Minus Zero teases an answer for in its second full-length trailer. It looks like viewers are in for pure carnage this time around, as the three-headed kaiju zaps any airborne structures out of the sky left and right. You can see how the sequel's returning human crew will "fight fire with fire" next month in the trailer below. Fight fire with fire. 🔥 #GodzillaMinusZero Godzilla Day IMAX Early Access on November 3. In theatres November 6. Tickets on sale now. https://t.co/2Ktmma6fOa https://t.co/U0NvFbnGL9 — GODZILLA.OFFICIAL (@Godzilla_Toho) October 11, 2026 With less than a month until its premiere, it seems the filmmakers behind the Godzilla Minus One sequel are going to save the full Ghidorah reveal for those who go to the theater. We'll at least know how the character has been redesigned for the Minus universe when it premieres November 6. Godzilla Minus Zero's NYCC presence wasn't just limited to this electrifying new trailer, though. Producer Kazuaki Kishida, visual effects artist and compositor Tatsuji Nojima, sound designer and Foley artist Natsuko Inoue, and production and post-production sound mixer Hisafumi Takeuchi all gathered in New York for a panel covering the sequel and how it came to be. IGN attended the talk and came away with a few highlights. Nojima, who walked away from Godzilla Minus One as the first Gen Z Oscar winner in the visual effects category, said his time working on the 2023 film started simply as a hobby before director Takashi Yamazaki took note of his abilities. Kishida joked, "I don't know if I'd have a job right now" if not for the 25-year-old VFX artist's work, but Nojima isn't the only younger member of the crew. "There are even younger team members on the Godzilla Minus Zero team – 22, 23," Kishida said via translator. "They're talented enough to be given an entire cut or a scene to manage on their own. Director Yamazaki really likes working with young talent. I think he's very open-minded, and he absorbs whatever fresh takes or new ways younger artists are approaching different problems, and how they're solving it. There isn't really an age hierarchy in his organization. Everyone works very collaboratively, and I think it's a very good environment for young artists to try and flex what they have." One VFX-packed scene that viewers have already caught in trailers sees Godzilla emerging from the ocean while chasing after a plane. Even short moments like this can be quite complicated to bring to life when skyscraper-sized monsters are involved. Godzilla Minus Zero's status as the first Japanese production filmed for IMAX only made the process more complex, which is why it's especially impressive that the ocean scene in question required 2 billion particles and was made by just two people. Meanwhile, the crew had to get especially creative when trying to imagine what creatures like Godzilla and Ghidorah would sound like in real life . In Godzilla Minus One, the echo of its title kaiju's unmistakable roar was recorded by capturing audio of his voice in a baseball stadium. Introducing a new monster with Godzilla Minus Zero then took them to record audio in a dam. "I recall there were people having a picnic, maybe people just taking a stroll," Inoue said. "The person walking their dog, though, they had the worst time because the dog was freaking out and barking back at us." It'll all come together in just a few short weeks. In the meantime, you can see why IGN gave Godzilla Minus One an 8/10 . We've also already got a review for Godzilla Minus Zero, and you can see why we gave it a 7/10 here .

items.title: Naruto Teasers Reveal New Shadow Rising Manga and Anime Crossover Series
items.excerpt: Naruto is alive and well, as author Masashi Kishimoto has announced a new manga called Shadow Rising – and a new anime crossover series is on the way, too.
items.content_text: Naruto is alive and well, as author Masashi Kishimoto has announced a new manga called Shadow Rising – and a new anime crossover series is on the way, too. Both Naruto projects were announced during the Naruto panel at New York Comic Con 2026. Details about the manga, specifically, were light, with only Kishimoto's involvement and its "Shadow Rising" title confirmed for now. The panel did come with more information about that anime series, though. Aptly titled "Naruto x Ninku," the show will serve as a full-on crossover between Naruto and popular '90s manga and anime franchise Ninku . Both the show and the manga did receive teaser trailers, which you can see below. A teaser for new NARUTO manga by Masashi Kishimoto is here! Stay tuned for more updates at the NARUTO Super Stage at Jump Festa 2027! #PROJECT_RASENGAN #NARUTO #JumpFesta https://t.co/EseP4OSffI — NARUTO OFFICIAL (@NARUTO_info_en) October 10, 2026 Two legendary shinobi series collide. Fully supervised by Koji Kiriyama and Masashi Kishimoto, NARUTO x NINKŪ is in production! Director: Noriyuki Abe Character Designer / Chief Animation Director: Tetsuya Nishio https://t.co/d9fv6N2g86 #PROJECT_RASENGAN #NARUTO #NINKU https://t.co/VExZf7MTeJ — NARUTO OFFICIAL (@NARUTO_info_en) October 10, 2026 "Team 7 members Naruto, Sasuke, and Sakura are given a mission by Kakashi," an official description for Naruto x Ninku said. "Since Kakashi cannot participate himself, Naruto is appointed acting leader. As a result of this decision, Naruto is fully motivated to make the mission a success. However, on the way, Team 7 finds themselves lost in another world. What appears before the bewildered trio is a boy with a face resembling a frog’s, named Fūsuke. What awaits them in this strange new world?" Meanwhile, as reported by Variety , the Naruto panel also came with a surprise update on the live-action movie . Amid rumors of early plot details and casting decisions, director Destin Daniel Cretton shared a message where he explained "what an honor it is to bring Kishimoto-sensei's incredible world and characters to life." "The further we get into making this film, the more excited I am about what we’re creating," he continued. "What I’ve always loved about Naruto is that he’s the character who might normally get sidelined as a sidekick. He’s excitable, he tries too hard, and people underestimate him. But he has an incredible heart. No matter how many times he fails or gets knocked down, he never stops believing in himself or fighting for the people he loves. That spirit is at the heart of the story we’re telling. "These characters mean so much to so many people, myself included, and I carry that with me as we make this film. We’re approaching the world, relationships, and journeys Kishimoto-sensei created with a lot of care, and we want to capture what makes NARUTO so special. We’re hard at work and will have more to share soon. Until then, thank you for your passion, your patience, and for being along for the ride. I can’t wait for you to see what’s ahead!" A description in the YouTube upload for Shadow Rising promised more details will be shared at the Naruto Super Stage at Jump Festa 2027. The Naruto x Ninku upload , meanwhile, confirmed that the show is in production with supervision from Kishimoto and Ninku author Koji Kiriyama, with the Naruto X/Twitter account confirming Noriyuki Abe as its director and Tetsuya Nishio as its character designer/chief animation director. Release date details remain a mystery for now.

items.title: Blade Runner 2099 Trailer Teases Replicant Mystery With Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh
items.excerpt: Prime Video has published a new Blade Runner 2099 trailer, revealing more about the mystery surrounding its missing Replicants, as well as the roles Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh play in the story.
items.content_text: Prime Video has published a new Blade Runner 2099 trailer, revealing more about the mystery surrounding its missing Replicants, as well as the roles Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh play in the story. This more detailed look at the Amazon-backed limited series and its dystopian sci-fi setting arrived at New York Comic Con 2026. Attendees at the Blade Runner 2099 panel were treated to the new trailer in person, with both it and a new poster now available for all to see online. Starring Schafer (Euphoria) and Yeoh (Everything Everywhere All at Once) as Cora and Olwen, respectively, Blade Runner 2099 is set to premiere in November. You can see the NYCC 2026 trailer below. A new world. A new order. A new Blade Runner. Blade Runner 2099, a new limited series, premieres November 25th on Prime Video. https://t.co/03OicCMpKl — prime video IN (@PrimeVideoIN) October 10, 2026 "Fifty years after the events of Blade Runner 2049, Los Angeles has been reborn, just not by humanity," an official description from Prime Video said. "Cora, a fugitive in a final bid to stop running, takes on one last identity: a Blade Runner. Forced to partner with Olwen, a Replicant days from dying, she hunts down a runaway hiding a truth that could collapse a fragile city." Today's comic-con trailer fills in some of the blanks left by the teaser revealed at San Diego Comic-Con this past July. Set 50 years after Ryan Gosling's Blade Runner 2049 and 80 years after Harrison Ford's original movie, Yeoh's Olwen can be heard saying 10 female and 18 male Replicants have gone missing in the last year. Amid tense words from Schafer's character, viewers are told that a mysterious "he" is out there, and he "knows the cure for all Replicants." "I don't know what you're doing," Yeoh's Olwen says as the trailer closes. "Do you?" The Blade Runner 2099 NYCC 2026 trailer provided a closer look into a mystery that certainly looks like it will fit in with past entries, but we'll have to wait until its November 25, 2026, release date to see how all of the pieces will come together. Its binge release plan will see all eight episodes available to stream on the same day. With both Ridley Scott's '80s original film and Denis Villeneuve's legacy sequel enjoying a dedicated following to this day, there's already a lot of hype behind Blade Runner 2099. For more while we wait, you can read IGN's new NYCC interview with showrunner Silka Luisa .

items.title: Arc Raiders' 2.0 Update and 'Spider-Man' Grappling Hook Drive Player Count to Reach 7-Month High
items.excerpt: The new Arc Raiders 2.0 update has triggered a seven-month high for its concurrent player count on Steam as fans show up for its "Spider-Man" grappling hook, a new map, a free weekend, and more.
items.content_text: The new Arc Raiders 2.0 update has triggered a seven-month high for its concurrent player count on Steam as fans show up for its "Spider-Man" grappling hook, a new map, a free weekend, and more. Embark's once-viral extraction experience has had a rough few months. As the studio slowed down updates and vowed to rework its divisive Expedition prestige system , Arc Raiders players have largely left it behind, hoping to one day return to Speranza should more enticing updates arrive. After reaching an all-time peak of nearly 500,000 players on Steam (via SteamDB ), it's consistently struggled to reach more than 35,000 players on PC since July. It was a fall from grace that's left fans missing the honeymoon phase, but the Frozen Trail update, which launched two days ago, October 8, across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S, has almost immediately brought back some of that hype. In September, Arc Raiders reached a player count low of just 10,000 on Steam. As of the publication of this story, 166,670 people are logged onto Arc Raiders on the PC platform alone, and it looks like it could keep climbing. It's a number Embark hasn't hit since early April, and although it's too soon to tell if these are the kind of results needed to give it a proper second wind, it does mark the first time the game has achieved a notable spike since December 2025. It's all thanks to Frozen Trail and the free weekend that helped usher it in. The update, which brought the first substantial changes Arc Raiders has received since Riven Tides in April , introduced a collection of game-changing content. Its crown jewel is Pendola Pass, a snowy mountainous region located beyond Raiders' usual home in the Rust Belt. New buildings to loot and shoot through would surely be enough to bring fans back, but it's really just the tip of the iceberg. New Arc threats like the Bully, Skulker, and Hydra have shaken up combat encounters. The Tether Launcher, which can tie enemies to objects against their will, and the Grappling Hook have given players new tools to experiment with. That aforementioned free weekend, meanwhile, which runs from October 8 – 12, has allowed even newcomers to check out how Embark has changed Arc Raiders for the better. Individually, these are updates that would pique the interest of even the most casual fan, but the only reason so many are installing the game again is because of how these tweaks add new toys to the sandbox. I was not a believer. This is one of the best updates ever in a video game. by u/Artistic_Annual8918 in ARC_Raiders "I was not a believer," one popular post on Reddit said . "This is one of the best updates ever in a video game." The same post continued, first praising Frozen Trail's scale. They admitted to being a lapsed Arc Raiders fan, explaining that the mix of Embark's new elements not only got them to return but also has them looking forward to what's next. "I absolutely loved Arc Raiders for its first 6 months but I got frustrated with it since they announced the twice a year update," they said. "I quit playing, said that these devs don’t know what they’re doing, they fumbled, etc. I know it probably won’t reach the popularity and number of players it had in December but that doesn’t matter to me, what matters to me is that I was flat out wrong about these devs and their ability to update the game. What they did here is special and I just wanted to come out and admit I was wrong and give them their flowers. I’m now extremely excited for the future of this game." While not everyone is willing to go as far as to call it an all-time great video game update, it's hard to find anyone being too critical of what Embark had to offer. Pendola Pass' size seems to be an especially notable bright spot, with others mentioning the new UFO-style Arc ship known as the Frigate as another big highlight. Managed to get on the frigate it's no joke up there like a destiny raid by u/cybrsloth92 in ARC_Raiders The FRIGATE in ARC Raiders is enormous! How are we supposed to fight this thing? 😭 📽️ u/cybrsloth92 https://t.co/w2HHvCDEkK — ARC Raiders Alerts (@ArcRaiderAlerts) October 8, 2026 "Just played an hour before work, and I couldn't even explore more than 15% of the map," one player said . "There were so many things to check out and explore, this time they really delivered a big map!" "I agree, not to mention the new weapons, skills, weapons mods, it’s hard to believe they did all this in less than 6 months. Frigate is so damn cool," another said . With such a drastic and sudden increase in attention, more highlight reels have started to find their way back to social media, too. New tools like the Grappling Hook come with obvious opportunities for shareable clips, as it allows Raiders to attach to everything from steep cliffs to flying Arc. Others can't help but draw comparisons to how the toy allows players to swing through maps like "Spider-Man." "I was going to get that," one fan said , referring to a new wall-running skill, "but then I remembered grappling hooks exist now. It's sooo much more fun to swing around like Spider-Man and then run around at 100mph with no stamina usage." There's also the new Advanced Camera. It works exactly how you'd expect, giving players the tech to capture memories, all with the click of a button. Considering Arc Raiders has thrived on the comedy presented by its in-game systems, a camera has really only given that chaos another chance to shine. ARC RAIDERS LETS YOU SWING LIKE SPIDER-MAN WITH THE NEW GRAPPLE HOOK! 🎥MisterMediocre https://t.co/XM22wmv5RZ — ARC Now (@ArcRaidersNow) October 9, 2026 Bullying a Rocketeer in ARC Raiders using the new grappling hook 😂 📽️ u/BranandWiller https://t.co/q8Q0AYUSzm — ARC Raiders Alerts (@ArcRaiderAlerts) October 10, 2026 THIS IS WHY ARC RAIDERS’ NEW CAMERA FEELS SO GOOD 🎥JojoBobaguard https://t.co/5xvYzcdVfN — ARC Now (@ArcRaidersNow) October 8, 2026 Arc Raiders is having a bit of a moment, but we'll have to see if it has truly managed to recapture the magic that made it such a hit at launch. Up next is testing for a dedicated PvE mode , something fans have begged to see implemented since launch. Embark is certainly at least trying, with the game also available for 50% off on all platforms as players flock to its free weekend. IGN gave Arc Raiders a 9/10 review when it arrived almost exactly one year ago, saying, "With polished gunplay and an irresistible grind, Arc Raiders sets a new standard for extraction shooters." Even if Embark can't entertain a consistently high number of players, it's clear the studio has more plans for the IP in the future. Both it and the studio's game-show-inspired FPS, The Finals, are set to receive TV show and movie adaptations at some point in the future . Frozen Trail brought more new content to Arc Raiders than we could list. You can see the full patch notes below. Arc Raiders Frozen Trail Update 2.0 Patch Notes Raiders! The cold has arrived, and it's brought a lot with it. Frozen Trail is our biggest update since launch, packed with new features, fresh challenges, and a long list of fixes and improvements. We've been working on this one for a while, and we couldn't be more excited to finally put it in your hands. Whether you're here for the new content or just want to know what we've fixed, there's something for everyone. Grab something warm, settle in, and read on for the full breakdown. Thank you for playing, for reporting bugs, and for sticking with us. Highlights New Map - Pendola Pass New Map Conditions - Frigate & Redirection New Enemies - Bully, Skulker, Hydra New Weapons - Bantam & Stiletto Amplified Weapons Revamped Skill Tree New Items - Grappling Hook, Basic & Advanced Cameras, Tether Launcher, Yank Grenade, Mountaineer’s Detector, Banjo & Harmonica The Outpost, including a new Research Bench Lootable “Design” items that unlock craftable Outpost furniture Quest System improvements, 22 new quests added New Reward Pass system Weapon Stencils Updated default gamepad mapping Reworked Map Selection screen, including visual and usability improvements Collector DLC is available now Max Stash Size increased by 2 new levels (328 Max without Expedition bonuses) Skill Tree Revamp Changes to the Raider Skill Tree include new skills and improvements to existing skills, enabling players to better embellish their playstyle with more impactful skill choices. We've heard the comments (and seen in the data) that the Skill Tree was not living up to its role in offering sufficiently interesting ways of building your character to better define and refine your playstyle. The goal of the Skill Tree revamp is twofold: to look at under-performing skills, modify or replace them, and to get closer to the goal of making choice and expression a more core feature of the Skill Tree. Alongside some new skills and a reshuffling of the layout, new functionality has been added to replace the previous 'large' nodes at the middle and end of the branches. Now, for the middle of each branch, instead of having two selectable skills and two 'paths', there is one path where the node is a binary choice between two skills. You can only choose one; you will be able to make the choice again when you reset your skill tree. At the end of each branch are two nodes where you must make a choice out of three skills. Here, you can choose up to two of the three, after reaching the required skill point investment. As this is a fairly big reimagining of the Skill Tree, there will likely be more tweaks and updates in the near future, to existing and new skills, as we see how you are engaging with it. Weapon Stencils The Frozen Trail update introduces Weapon Stencils, a new cosmetic option that lets players personalize the look of their weapons with a range of stencil patterns. Note that stenciled weapons can still be lost like any other weapon: if you're downed, other Raiders can loot your weapon along with its stencil. 14 Weapon Stencils: 5 Stencils are exclusive to Frozen Trail Premium Pass 1 Stencil is exclusive to DLC 8 Stencils can be found Topside Stencils are similar to blueprints, once learned you can apply them to compatible weapons. Applying Stencils requires Stencil Parts, which can be found Topside. Outpost New Outpost can be unlocked by completing a project. Remember to accept the quest and bring your camera! Outpost can be expanded with different modules Unlocking the outpost will unlock access to the research station Furniture Designs: Similar to blueprints, they can be learned and used to craft different furniture for your Outpost. 100 Furniture Designs have been added to the game 4 Furniture Designs are exclusive to Frozen Trail Pass 1 Furniture Design is exclusive to DLC 73 Furniture Designs can be found Topside 22 Furniture Designs are unlocked by upgrading the Outpost Reward Pass The Reward Pass is our new progression system and the evolution of Raider Decks. Alongside this change, Cred has been removed from the game and replaced by Reward Points, a new currency that's automatically applied toward your progress on whichever pass you currently have active. The first new pass is the Frozen Trail Pass, featuring 60 levels across a Free and a Premium track. Your existing Raider Decks haven't gone anywhere. They've been moved into the new Legacy Pass, and any rewards you've already unlocked are kept and will appear as granted. You can continue progressing through the Legacy Pass at any time by setting it as your active pass. Note that only one Reward Pass can be active at a time, so your Reward Points will go toward whichever pass you've selected. Feats Rework Feats are now split into 3 different categories: Easy, Medium and Hard. Easy: 15 Reward Points, +1 weekly milestone progression Medium: 25 Reward Points, +2 weekly milestone progression Hard: 50 Reward Points, +3 weekly milestone progression. Weekly milestones are granting 250 Reward Points each, there are 3 of them available per week: Milestone 1: Get 4 weekly milestone progress Milestone 2: Get 8 weekly milestone progress Milestone 3: Get 12 weekly milestone progress After completing your weekly milestones, you can keep completing Feats, but no major milestone rewards will be granted until the weekly timer is reset. Twitch Drops You can grab some new backpack attachments by watching your favorite streamer play ARC Raiders! You’ll need to watch at least 60 minutes to receive the Oxygen Respirator, and 120 minutes for the Mailbox. These drops will be live between October 8 - November 4, 2026. Content and Bug Fixes Animation Knockback animations now align with the actual direction you’re pushed in. Fixed an issue where, after reconnecting and being revived, your character could jitter and display broken animations while moving. Fixed an issue where you could get stuck on small obstacles when sliding. Added animations to show the player interacting with their map and inventory. Added mouth animation for when players are talking in proximity chat. Added new contextual character animations; like exhaustion when running out of breath for a while and brushing off dust after sliding. Fixed an issue where players kept some items in their hands during the knockout animation or during some interactions. Additional animation polish and tweaks. ARC Adjusted the multi-target laser from the Vaporizer to give players a clearer window for dodging with fast traversal and dodge mechanics. Added fire status effect visuals for ARC drones. Moved higher tier loot from the armor pieces of the legs to the legs pieces for Queen and Matriarch. The armor plates are supposed to protect the legs, so it made sense to relocate the loot to the protected area. Having the loot inside the armor took away from the experience and was inconsistent with how other ARC work. Armor pieces can still contain some loot. Improved AI sight handling to prevent rare detection errors in enemy awareness. The Matriarch can once again use all of its ranged attacks. Rebalanced physical force effects against certain ARC enemies. Audio Adjusted how character sounds are occluded by walls and obstacles for more natural audio positioning. Added more variations to metal groan sound effects to improve environmental ambience. Added missing sound effects to the Snap Hook for attaching, detaching, and rope movement to improve audio feedback. Updated the sound for Skill Tree unlocks and added a hold-interaction audio cue in the UI. Fixed an issue where some weapon sounds could fail to play. Improved the quality of the Raider Voice model, providing a higher fidelity of voice conversion. Cosmetic Updated Celeste’s appearance . Added an Emissive Toggle for backpacks with light sources. That means you can now turn off the lights from your favorite backpacks to go full stealth mode. The Zenith Outfit now has all of its intended toggles. Players who own the outfit will receive the missing toggles shortly. Gameplay “Solo vs. Squads” is no longer available in the matchmaking options. We want players to have a proper incentive to use all of the available matchmaking settings, which Solo vs. Squads currently lacks. To that end, we're taking time to re-evaluate its role in the game. Reworked the explosive damage formula for ARC. In practice this means that explosive weapons like the Hullcracker will deal over 50% more damage against armor plates but around 30% less damage against more fragile parts. The intention is to make explosive damage feel more consistent across the board as well as increasing its effectiveness against heavy armor. Since most ARC are heavily armored and we want the numeric damage output to be more consistent this also means that its effectiveness against weak points is slightly reduced. Made certain changes to skills that were in the previous Skill Tree iteration to fit them better within the new one: Stamina gained from Fight or Flight increased by ~25% per level. Stubborn Mule stamina regen values increased by ~33%. Increase Back on Your Feet healing from 30 to 40. Added more contextual Ping information for ARC and various objects. The Stash can be upgraded further, by two tiers. The new maximum (without Expedition rewards or acquired Nomadic Envoy space) is 328 slots. You can now drop loot to the ground directly from containers You can no longer sprint-climb ladders when exhausted Addressed some instances where vaulting onto destroyed ARC parts or other movable surfaces could unexpectedly launch or shove the player. Weapon slot weight reduction now applies only to the loadout; other containers and sub-containers are unaffected. You can now open the map while downed. Improved hit registration when shooting while on top of ARC. Heavy Shield: reduced durability decay from 0.20 to 0.15 and decreased movement penalty while equipped from 15% to 10%. Added Scrambling. Sprinting at steep slopes will allow you to scramble up them for a short time. You now automatically enter a sliding state after tumbling for too long. Items Increased Flame Spray range to better match its visual effect and improve usability. Ziplines now break when intersecting something after being placed. Reduced Snap Hook range from 20m to 18m, increased durability consumption from 2% to 4% per use, and raised power cost from 50 to 60. As we added more personal mobility items, it became clear we needed to begin differentiating them to a greater degree. While the Snap Hook has previously been a ‘general use’ mobility gadget, with the introduction of the Grappling Hook, we felt the need to give them their own identity outside of a ‘linear upgrade’ path. With these changes, we aim to make the Snap Hook better fit its role as being a burst mobility gadget; something that is used to quickly close distance or traverse a location, but with more commitment when doing so. The power cost increase will still allow for multiple uses within a short time when at full power, but will no longer allow for immediate back-to-back uses. Fixed an issue where items were appearing outside their intended areas or containers. These items will now only be available within their designated locations. Weapons Updated Anvil’s rarity from Green to Blue. The Anvil has been a tricky weapon to evaluate. It comes with a versatility that allows it to effectively take on both Raiders and ARC alike, and is outperforming weapons both within and above its own level of rarity. But it is also a fan-favourite and a staple of the game in its own way. We felt that increasing the rarity level for it would put it in a better place within the economy, while still maintaining the gameplay and power that we know and love. In its place, the Bantam will take the role of the uncommon hand cannon, with a balance that is more suitable for the role. The Anvil Splitter is no longer usable as a mod, and it has now become an improved upgrade option for the Amplified Anvil. We have also removed the Tech Mod slot from the Anvil to reflect this. The item itself should no longer drop, but will remain in the game for a while, allowing players to sell or recycle it into Amplified Fragments used for repairing Amplified Weapons. Fixed an unintended behavior where the Jupiter's damage would propagate twice to ARC parts behind its intended target. As a result, the Jupiter is now stronger against armor, but slightly weaker against weak spots. The Hullcracker will no longer appear incomplete when inspected in the menu. Fixed an issue where the Dolabra would not destroy the yellow weak points inside the Harvester. Fixed an issue where weapons picked up from the ground appeared without their attached parts. Maps Improved alignment of Doorblockers (now vertical) for small side-sliding-doors. Improved texture quality on several maps, resolving blocky and inconsistent visuals. Fixed areas on several maps where players could get stuck on terrain while in a Downed state. Some areas on the edges of maps are darker than intended. Blue Gate Adjusted lighting on…

items.title: Image Comics' Roam Reunites Paper Girls Creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang
items.excerpt: In one of the coolest announcements to come out of NYCC, IGN can exclusively reveal that Paper Girls creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang are reuniting for a new series called Roam.
items.content_text: In what is easily one of the most exciting comic book-related announcements to come out of NYCC 2026, IGN can exclusively reveal that Paper Girls creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang are reuniting for a new project at Image Comics. That series is called Roam, and it's their first collaboration in over a decade. See the cover art for Roam #1 below: The creative team on Roam also includes colorist Matt Wilson and letterer Jared Fletcher. Here's the official description for Roam: In the future, everyone gets to be a superhero… but only while you’re young. From the Eisner Award-winning team behind Paper Girls, ROAM reunites Saga writer Brian K. Vaughan and Catwoman: Lonely City creator Cliff Chiang for their first new ONGOING SERIES in over a decade. Exploring the power and peril that comes with new adulthood, ROAM is a timeless adventure about the quest we each take in life to finally find our team. The action-packed 50-page (!!!) first issue arrives in comic stores this February 2027! “Cliff has already drawn the first several issues of ROAM, and I can’t wait for readers to see this breathtakingly original world he and our gifted collaborators Matt and Jared helped create," Vaughan tells IGN. "Thanks so much to the readers and retailers out here who are up for exploring something new with us!" "There's no bigger thrill than breathing life into new worlds with your friends, that electric feeling of collaboration," Chiang says. "ROAM is unlike anything Brian and I have done before, but inspired by our love for comics as a medium. It's been a joy to reunite with our trusted teammates Matt Wilson and Jared Fletcher, and I'm incredibly grateful to Image Comics for continuing the creative partnership and exploration that began with Paper Girls. It's going to be a wild ride!" Roam #1 will be released in February 2027, and it's already shaping up to be one of our most anticipated new comics of the eyar. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop . For more, check out IGN's original review of Paper Girls #1 and our review of Paper Girls Season 1 . Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .
